title: The leaders want the room
text: After a sloppy week on the track, the leadership group has called a players-only meeting about what it means to wear the red and white. They've asked you to stay out.

choices.label: Leave it to the leaders

effects.why: The players set their own standard
The group sorted it out among themselves

effects.hit_result: It turned into a blame session and a few players walked out flat.

choices.result: The door shuts. You hear raised voices, then quiet.

choices.label: Sit in the back of the room

effects.why: The leaders said their piece with the coach there

choices.result: The leaders speak well. The young blokes don't say a word.

title: Is he a Swans person?
text: The recruiters love a gifted midfielder who is there for the taking, but every reference check says the same thing: late to training, hard work off the field, sulks when dropped. The leaders want to know if he fits.

choices.label: Bring him in and fix him

effects.why: A known bad trainer joined the group

effects.hit_result: By midseason he's still the same bloke, and the group has noticed.

choices.result: He signs. The board likes the talent; the leaders reserve judgement.

choices.label: Not our type of player

effects.why: The club turned down talent that didn't fit

choices.result: He goes elsewhere. The leaders nod; the board watched the talent walk past.

title: The culture under the microscope
text: A report of misbehaviour at a team function has reached the papers, and pundits are asking whether the famous Swans culture was ever real. The board wants a response today.

choices.label: Open an independent review

effects.why: The club let outsiders hold it to account

choices.result: The review starts. The questions don't stop for weeks.

choices.label: Handle it in-house

effects.why: The group closed ranks

effects.hit_result: More came out a week later, and the board was not impressed.

choices.result: The club says little. The players pull tight.

choices.label: Front the media yourself
choices.result: You take every question. You're the story for a week, not them.

title: Cheer, cheer the red and the white
text: {name} has played his first game and you've won. Tradition says the debutant stands in the middle of the rooms and leads the song. He's terrified.

choices.label: Into the middle, son

effects.why: The whole room sang with the new kid

effects.hit_result: He fluffed the words, the footage got out and the papers had their fun.

choices.result: {first} gets through it, just. The room goes up.

choices.label: Let the captain lead it this week

effects.why: You spared him on his first night
A club ritual was skipped

choices.result: The captain leads it. {first} sings from the back, relieved.

title: The ugliest footy in the league
text: A Melbourne commentator says your pressure game is the ugliest footy going and is killing the game in a rugby league town. The marketing team wants a flashier brand.

choices.label: We play to win, not to entertain

effects.why: The club stuck to the way it plays

choices.result: The players love it. The sponsors wanted highlights.

choices.label: Open it up a bit
choices.result: The forwards get more room. The defence leaks while it learns.

title: Derby week
text: It's the Sydney Derby. The Giants have been saying the city is turning orange, and your older players remember when the Swans had Sydney to themselves.

choices.label: This is our town
choices.result: The group is fired up. The Giants have a new line for their noticeboard.

choices.label: Two clubs grow the game

effects.why: The coach stayed above the noise

choices.result: The league loves the answer. The members wanted some fire.

title: The fight for the west
text: The Giants have stepped up junior clinics in Western Sydney. The community department wants three senior players out there for a day to show the kids the Swans are their club too.

choices.label: Send three seniors

effects.why: The senior players went out west for the club

choices.result: The kids swarm the stars. The seniors come back tired.

choices.label: Send the rookies
choices.result: The rookies have a ball. Nobody out west knows who they are.

title: The Eagles again
text: Games against West Coast have a habit of coming down to a kick, and the players know it. The press calls it the closest rivalry going.

choices.label: Train for the last two minutes
choices.result: A week of close-game drills. It's a hard week on the legs.

choices.label: Treat it as any other game
choices.result: A normal week. Some of the group feel the occasion was undersold.

title: Do the Hawks have our number?
text: The papers are running the old line that Hawthorn beat Sydney when it matters, and a senior player admits the group carries it.

choices.label: Name it and bury it

effects.why: The group faced the Hawthorn question head on

choices.result: It's out in the open. Now the group has to back it up.

choices.label: There's no hoodoo

effects.why: The coach kept the focus on this week's job

choices.result: You brush it off in the press. Some of the players aren't so sure.

title: Scared of black and white?
text: The Magpie army will fill the ground, and a radio host asks whether the Swans are scared of Collingwood. The old bogey talk is back.

choices.label: Change the plan for them
choices.result: A new plan for one opponent. The group is still learning it at the first bounce.

choices.label: Back our game

effects.why: The club trusted its own game against the Pies

choices.result: Same plan, same players. If it goes wrong, the talk gets louder.

title: The cricket's on
text: The cricket has the SCG locked up, so the side is training at a suburban ground with a bumpy surface and no gym on site. The players are grumbling.

choices.label: Bus them to a proper facility
choices.result: Good work done, and an hour each way in Sydney traffic.

choices.label: Make do

effects.why: The group rolled its sleeves up on a rough ground

choices.result: Nobody loves the surface, but nobody whinges either.

title: A visit to the old South
text: The Melbourne supporters, many from old South Melbourne families, want the team to visit the old Lake Oval grandstand the day before the next game in Melbourne. It means a long afternoon on a short trip.

choices.label: Take them home

effects.why: The players saw where the club began

choices.result: The old South families are thrilled. The players are a bit tired.

choices.label: Hotel and recovery
choices.result: The legs are right for the game. The old supporters feel forgotten.

title: A game back in Melbourne
text: An old South Melbourne supporters' group has written to the board: the club has forgotten where it came from. They want one home game a year played in Melbourne.

choices.label: Give them a game in Melbourne

effects.why: The old South members got a home game back

choices.result: The old members are thrilled. The Sydney commercial team is not, and the side travels for a home game.

choices.label: We're Sydney now

effects.why: The old South members felt cut loose

choices.result: Every home game stays at the SCG. The letter goes in a drawer.

title: Up the road to the Riverina
text: The league wants a practice match in the Riverina, the heartland of footy in New South Wales. Big crowd, small ground, long bus trip.

choices.label: Take the best side

effects.hit_result: A hard country ground took a toll on the best players.

choices.result: The town turns out. The kids get their photos with the stars.

choices.label: Send a development side
choices.result: The young blokes get a run. The locals wanted the stars.

title: A rugby league town
text: The back pages are wall-to-wall rugby league this week. The media team says you'll get nothing unless a player does something eye-catching, like a beach photo shoot with a league star.

choices.label: Do the shoot

hit.why: The group saw the shoot as a sideshow

choices.result: The Swans make the paper. A half-day goes on the beach.

choices.label: Let the footy do the talking

effects.why: The club kept its mind on football

choices.result: Nothing in the papers. The commercial team wanted the exposure.

title: Beach or gym?
text: It's a heatwave and the beach is five minutes away. The players want to swap a gym session for an ocean swim and a coffee at Bondi. The fitness staff say the program is the program.

choices.label: Beach session
choices.result: Salt water and a flat white. The gym work waits.

choices.label: Gym as planned
choices.result: The work gets done. It's 38 degrees and everyone knows it.

title: Our own Sydney kid
text: A Sydney junior the club has coached since he was fourteen is now rated by rival recruiters. To be sure of him, you'd have to spend your first pick well before most clubs would take him.

choices.label: Take him with our first pick

effects.why: The club kept its own Sydney kid

choices.result: He stays home. A higher-rated player goes elsewhere.

choices.label: Gamble he slides to our second pick

hit.why: The juniors staff watched their kid go to a rival

effects.hit_result: A rival took him first. The juniors staff are crushed.
effects.miss_result: He slid to your second pick, and the first went on the best player left.

choices.result: You hold your nerve on draft night.

title: Were they gifts?
text: Rival club bosses say the league's help for the northern clubs hands Sydney cheap stars and an easier pay packet. A journalist asks whether your best young players were gifts.

choices.label: We pay for every one of them

effects.hit_result: The league took a harder line, and the board blamed the noise.

choices.result: Sydney is expensive, you say; ask any player. It runs all week.

choices.label: It's the league's call

effects.why: The coach kept out of a fight with the league

choices.result: The story dies. The young players heard their coach didn't defend them.

title: Luring a star north
text: A star forward at a Melbourne club is tempted by the harbour and a long contract. Getting him means a huge offer, and the leaders are asking if one player is worth it.

choices.label: Go all in

choices.result: He signs on the harbour. The cap is squeezed and the change rooms notice.

choices.label: Walk away

effects.why: The club kept the list balanced

choices.result: He goes elsewhere. The members wanted the splash.

title: The go-home factor
text: {name} is homesick. His family is on the other side of the country, the Sydney rent is brutal and his manager is hinting at a trade home.

choices.label: Extend him now, with help on housing

effects.why: You backed him with a new deal

choices.result: {first} signs on. Others on the list want the same deal.

choices.label: Give him a week at home

hit.why: He still asked about a trade home

effects.hit_result: He came back and still asked about a trade.

choices.result: {first} flies home and comes back brighter.

choices.label: Let the manager shop him

effects.why: The group watched a teammate shopped around

choices.result: The manager makes calls. The club will get something back.

title: The West Australian connection
text: The recruiters say the best value in this draft is in Western Australia. The list manager points out the last batch of West Australians all went home.

choices.label: Back the WA kids

hit.why: One of the WA kids asked to go home

choices.result: A strong haul from the west. Time will tell if they stay.

choices.label: Stay local and northern

effects.why: The club backed its own juniors

choices.result: The juniors staff are happy. The crop is a little weaker.

title: The league's flagship
text: League headquarters wants to move a home game to a midweek night to fill a prime-time slot in the Sydney market. It leaves a five-day break.

choices.label: Do it for the game
choices.result: The league is grateful. The legs aren't.

choices.label: Ask to keep the weekend slot
choices.result: The weekend game stays. The league remembers who said no.

effects.why: Nobody is bigger than the club

title: A Brownlow club
text: The club has produced more Brownlow medallists than most. A club legend and former medallist offers to talk to the midfield about doing the team things that win votes.

choices.label: Have him in

effects.why: A medallist showed the mids how it's done

choices.result: An afternoon of stories. The mids hang on every word.

choices.label: Keep the focus on the game plan

title: Booed on every ground
text: One of your Indigenous players has been booed at every away game for weeks. He isn't sleeping and has asked for a week off. The media can't stop talking about it.

choices.label: Stand with him, publicly

effects.why: The club stood beside one of its own

choices.result: The club speaks up. A week of headlines follows, and the group is right behind him.

choices.label: Give him the week, say little

effects.why: The group wanted the club to speak up

choices.result: He gets his week away. The players wanted more from the club.

choices.label: Play him; footy is the answer
choices.result: He plays. The week runs as planned, but he isn't right.
